subject: Discovery follow-up: context window budget, streaming requirements & traffic-shaping
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@integrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's call

Evan / Alejandra — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Highlights from discovery:
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end generation under 300ms for short queries (~<1k input tokens), with an aspirational 150–200ms for critical UI flows.
- Throughput profile: steady-state ~250 req/s, with peaks up to ~800 req/s for scheduled syncs. Concurrency per session expected 1–3; burstiness primarily from batch ingestion.
- Streaming: client requires streaming token-by-token for live transcription and incremental UI updates. Must support SSE/WebSocket style streaming; minimal startup jitter tolerated.
- Context sizing: typical user interactions ~1k tokens input, but some diagnostic exports may push input windows to 12k tokens (docs + context). Output ceilings: normal UI responses 128–256 tokens; long-form summaries up to 2k tokens (rare).
- Failure modes: if full-context requests hit latency SLO, they'd prefer graceful degradation (truncated backfill or fallback to cached summary) vs returning errors.

Key constraints we flagged on our side:
- Long input windows (8k–12k tokens) will increase per-request compute and may push some model variants beyond 300ms at p95; streaming mitigations help but KV-cache and prefix caching will be important.
- For sustained 800 req/s peaks with 12k inputs we recommend dedicated reserved pools vs hosted burst mode.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Integra to send representative payloads (3 examples: UI query, batch export, transcript) — see attached sample_payloads.json.
2) Redwood to run an initial perf sweep (latency + streaming startup) against two model+quantization combos and share p50/p95 numbers. (ETA: 5 business days after payload receipt.)
3) Tentative PoC: 2-week dedicated environment for peak/soak test + streaming verification. We'll include KV-prefix caching and a streaming client sample.
4) Decision workshop with Eng + Product to agree on acceptable graceful degradation patterns (truncate vs cached summary) — propose Wed 10/14.

Attachments: Integra_PoC_Requirements.pdf (PoC scope), sample_payloads.json (examples)

If that aligns, I'll loop in Karthik for perf plan and Marissa for commercial/SLAs.

Thanks — Soojin

--

Thanks Soojin — this is perfect and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 12k token exports will be infrequent (maybe 1–2 per hour at most) but non-negotiable for some compliance workflows. If there's a clear fallback path that preserves the gist, that would work.
- Streaming is required for the live note-taking UI — p95 for first token is the most important metric there.
- For the PoC, can Redwood include a simple client we can drop into our front-end to validate SSE vs WebSocket behavior?

We'll attach a sanitized transcript and 3 payload examples by end of day tomorrow. Also looping in Alejandra here for scheduling.

Karthik / Marissa — brief context: Integra needs streaming-first UX with p95 first-token tightness, steady ~250rps and peaks to ~800rps, and occasional 12k-token input jobs. They prefer graceful degradation over outright failures. Payloads + sanitized transcript coming tomorrow.

Karthik, immediate asks for planning:

Marissa — can you flag any playbook items (intro to finance for reserve quotes) so we can time the PoC commitment?

Soojin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-07T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's call

Thanks for the summary. Quick technical plan and assumptions below.

Assumptions pulled from call:
- Typical interactive: 1k in / 128 out, streaming enabled.
- Heavy job: 12k in / 2k out (batched background job).
- Peak concurrency: 800 concurrent requests during ingest windows, but many are batch jobs that can tolerate slightly higher latency.

Perf sweep plan (minimal):
1) Models: run against two model families — a lower-latency quantized 7B variant and a 13/14B efficiency-tuned model.
2) Quantization: FP16 vs 4-bit QAT (we'll test Q4_0/Q4_1 depending on compatibility).
3) Tests: short interactive (1k/128 streaming), mid (4k/512), and heavy (12k/2k) with both single-request and batched modes. For streaming, measure first-byte latency (how long until token stream begins) and sustained per-token throughput.
4) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end, first-byte p50/p95, GPU utilization, memory footprint, KV cache hit % for repeated prefixes.
5) Run context-caching scenarios: full-send vs KV-cache-enabled vs prefix-truncated to see latency/quality tradeoffs.

Preliminary expectation: Hosted can meet interactive SLAs for 1k inputs with the smaller quantized model. For sustained 800rps peaks with frequent 12k jobs, Dedicated/reserved pools will likely be necessary to keep p95 under 300ms for the interactive path (we'll validate). Streaming startup is very sensitive to model load and network handshake — our sample client will help quantify handshake jitter.

Logistics & timeline:
- Send sample payloads (Integra) by 10/07 EOD -> Redwood will kick off sweep on 10/08 -> quick results by 10/13.
- PoC proposal (environment, sizing, cost) by 10/14.

Questions for Integra (short):
- Do the 12k inputs include attachments or are they purely text? (attachments often change tokenization strategy).
- Are you able to tolerate truncated context when we apply smart prefixing (e.g., keep last 3k tokens + compressed summary of earlier content)?

I'll attach a short checklist (Integra_perf_sweep_checklist.pdf) to this thread after this note.

-Karthik
